scope: Reconcile the MTEXT 250-character continuation rule with target-encoded DXF string limits and peer writer behavior; refine existing PAR-05/PAR-28/29 and 7M implementation readiness.

method.kind: Primary-format documentation and current open-source writer/parser review plus local source/test audit
localInspection: DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md: PAR-05, PAR-28/29, 7M, and existing control-character framing progress
src/libdxfrw.cpp: standalone writeMText and embedded writeEmbeddedMText
tests/dxf_fixture_tests.cpp: existing generated MTEXT tests and generic control-character boundary coverage
method.limitations: Autodesk's published wording does not define a universal byte-count unit for UTF-8, legacy code pages, or escape-expanded text. The reviewed ezdxf master URLs are mutable and were inspected as source only, not executed or pinned. LibreDWG #1408 is a reporter-authored external issue with no public failing drawing inspected here. Local findings are source/coverage observations; no runtime defect was reproduced.

evidence.topic: Autodesk MTEXT chunk contract and general DXF string limit are distinct
observed: The Autodesk MTEXT table places content below 250 characters entirely in group 1 and describes longer content as 250-character chunks in one or more group-3 records.
When group 3 is used, Autodesk says the final record is group 1 and has fewer than 250 characters.
The cited less-than / greater-than wording does not expressly assign the exactly-250-character case.

The general DXF group-code reference separately says string groups 1-4, 7, 9, and 300-309 have a 255-character maximum and less for Unicode; it does not reduce the MTEXT rule to a universal 250-byte rule.
doesNotEstablish: A single physical byte limit applicable identically to UTF-8, legacy code pages, and escaped Unicode output.
Exact native behavior for a continuation sequence at an exact multiple of 250 characters.
evidence.planUse: Keep character chunk accounting separate from encoded DXF string transport. Retain one group 1 at exactly 250 where target transport permits; for chunked content use a final group-1 tail shorter than 250 as the conservative documented shape, pending a matched native exact-multiple witness.

evidence.topic: ezdxf current source differs at exact multiples and exposes chunk reconstruction order
observed: export_mtext_content calls split_mtext_string with size 250, emits every chunk except the last as group 3, and emits the final chunk as group 1; empty text becomes one empty group 1.
split_mtext_string indexes Python string characters and adjusts a boundary only when the chunk would end in caret notation.
load_mtext_content gathers group-3 values in order and appends group 1 to reconstruct content.

An exact 500-character string can therefore be emitted as one 250-character group 3 and one 250-character group 1, which differs from Autodesk's stated final-group-1-shorter-than-250 wording when continuation tags are used.
doesNotEstablish: That Autodesk accepts or rejects every such exact-multiple profile.
Byte-safe behavior for all target encodings or complete MTEXT semantic/rendering parity.
An immutable peer source revision or an independent native witness.
evidence.planUse: Record the exact-multiple case as a peer divergence. Do not adopt the peer output as the expected wire form without a pinned native-produced/accepted control.

evidence.topic: LibreDWG #1408 is a framing test-design lead only
observed: The report says a literal CR inside text values can create an empty physical line where a DXF group code is expected and can drop the next text character in a LibreDWG 0.14 Windows output.
The reported source drawings were not public in the issue and no exact reproducer/fix was verified in this research pass.
doesNotEstablish: A libdxfrw defect or universal control-character serialization rule.
That every CR should be converted to caret notation or silently removed.
evidence.planUse: Extend existing generated PAR-05 coverage through standalone and embedded MTEXT, checking explicit newline/loss policy, physical ASCII framing, binary boundaries, following-record alignment, and destination preservation.

evidence.topic: Local route audit reveals the embedded/standalone and strict/compatible gaps
observed: dxfWriter::writeUtf8Chunks limits target-encoded bytes and protects strict UTF-8 scalar boundaries; that maxBytes value is not the Autodesk character count.
writeMText has separate strict and compatibility chunk branches, while writeEmbeddedMText currently emits the complete content with one group-1 write.
Existing control-character regression coverage verifies generic ASCII refusal/binary framing, but the MTEXT content-specific 250-boundary and logical-newline profiles remain distinct checks.
doesNotEstablish: A new production runtime failure from this read-only audit.
That bytes currently emitted by embedded MTEXT are independently accepted by a native writer/consumer.
evidence.planUse: Refine 7M to use one target-version-aware encoder/chunker for standalone and embedded MTEXT; extend existing generated ASCII/Binary DXF tests and preserve outer ATTRIB/ATTDEF framing and the PAR-05 generic owner.

ownersRefined: PAR-28/29 MTEXT chunking and explicit downgrade outcomes
7M shared standalone/embedded text encoding and generated ASCII/Binary boundary tests
readinessRefinement: Separate Autodesk's 250-character chunk wording from encoded DXF transport bounds; do not label 250 bytes as the standard.
Keep the exact-250 case explicit because the cited Autodesk MTEXT wording uses strict less-than and greater-than conditions.
Cover ASCII 249/250/251 and exact multiples 499/500/501, non-ASCII byte/character divergence, DBCS or escape boundaries, caret pairs, empty text, and exact group-code reconstruction.
Keep the final group-1 chunk shorter than 250 under the documented default; resolve the ezdxf exact-multiple divergence only with a pinned native compatibility observation.
Share one target-version-aware chunking path for standalone MTEXT and group-101 embedded MTEXT, including ATTRIB and ATTDEF.
Carry explicit LF/CRLF/bare-CR/literal-escape policy through ASCII and Binary DXF with following-record and publication-failure controls.
Use only the strict fixture target, focused selector/CTest, lc3_compat_check, and scoped diff checks per implementation slice; no full-suite or peer run added.
